title: When the Prom Sings
premise: Jude Whitlock, a nonbinary senior who runs a meticulous anonymous account exposing school corruption, is invited into a group chat called 'The Prom Sings' where members receive predictions of events that haven't happened yet — and every prediction comes true, including ones that implicate the school board in a buried scandal from three years ago: the cover-up of a student's death during a hazing ritual. As the predictions grow darker and the board begins hunting the chat's members, Jude must decide whether loyalty to their best friend Priya — whose brother was the student who died — matters more than the truth they've spent three years protecting. In the end, Jude sacrifices their anonymity at prom itself, broadcasting the board's buried records as the gymnasium lights fail, and the chat's final prediction — that the truth will sing — comes true as the school board resigns and Priya, though wounded by Jude's earlier silence, chooses to stand beside them.
about_author: Noor Marchetti is the pen name of a former debate coach who spent a decade watching teenagers out-argue adults and decided to write about it. They live in a coastal town that holds its grudges gracefully, and this is their second young adult novel.

chapters.title: The Careful Life
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. We meet Jude mid-senior-year: a coder who posts anonymously as @hallmonitor, exposing small school injustices with surgical care, never leaving a trace. Their only confidant is Priya, who doesn't know about the account. When a mysterious group chat invite appears with Jude's real name, the careful life cracks. Beat: dread disguised as control.

chapters.title: Six Members, No Sender
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The chat, 'The Prom Sings,' has six members — all students, all connected to the class of three years ago — and no one admits to creating it. The first prediction arrives: a fire drill at 11:42, which happens exactly. Priya notices Jude's distraction. Beat: fascination curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Predictions and Small Cruelties
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Theo, a football player in the chat who received a prediction about his own injury. The chat predicts a teacher's resignation, then a car accident in the parking lot — minor, but true. Members begin suspecting each other. Jude realizes the predictions orbit one fixed date: three years ago, October 14th. Beat: paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: What October Buried
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, grieving her brother Marcus's 'accidental' death three years ago, notices the chat's date and starts her own digging. Jude, terrified, lies to her about why. Meanwhile the school board quietly cancels the traditional senior assembly — the first prediction that hasn't come true, because someone intervened. Beat: grief and guilt braided together.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following a prediction that names a room, Jude and Theo break into the school's records archive and find a sealed incident report: Marcus died during a hazing ritual sanctioned by then-vice-principal and current board member Alan Voss. The report was buried; the file is corrupted — except someone in the chat seems to already know its contents. Beat: revelation as vertigo.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Locked Door
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Jude after finding @hallmonitor's drafts on a shared drive — Jude has known about the cover-up's edges for a year and said nothing, protecting the source and themselves. Priya's fury is devastating: 'You got to be careful. Marcus just got to be dead.' Beat: the cost of truth withheld from the people it belongs to.

chapters.title: The Board Moves First
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Voss identifies the chat members through a district IT audit; Theo is threatened with losing his scholarship and college recommendation unless he names the others. He almost does. The chat predicts its own exposure — and then a prediction arrives that terrifies Jude most: 'Prom will sing.' Beat: betrayal as temptation, resisted at cost.

chapters.title: Who Built the Choir
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude traces the chat's creation to Ms. Okafor, Marcus's former debate teacher, who has been feeding predictions she derived from Voss's own leaked emails — testing the students, assembling witnesses. She never predicted anything; she knew. The final 'prediction' is a choice she's handing them. Beat: the mystery resolves into responsibility.

chapters.title: Prom Will Sing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. Prom night. Voss, tipped off, moves to expel the chat members before diplomas are issued. Jude, with Priya — reconciliation still raw — hijacks the AV system during the prom's opening song and broadcasts the incident report, Voss's emails, and three years of @hallmonitor's archive to every phone in the gymnasium. Beat: the careful kid chooses exposure; the room goes silent, then doesn't.

chapters.title: Graduation
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, resolution. Voss resigns under investigation; the district reopens Marcus's case. Priya delivers the senior speech, naming her brother aloud for the first time in three years. Jude, no longer anonymous, stands in the crowd as Priya dedicates the speech to 'everyone who was careful when they should have been loud.' The chat goes quiet, its work done. Beat: grief honored, truth shared, memory kept.
